state.context:
Assess specification coherence for the two syntax updates the user has requested in canlang. Its product priority is adoption through concise tokens, dependable AI authorship and low complexity for CRUD company SaaS. Executable language tools and token/generation trials are absent. Preserve typed do scenarios, single-space lexical depth, explicit caller/trusted-source permissions and atomic guarded writes. No other borrowing or line-minimizing rewrite is included, and classifier advice does not authorize or veto the chosen updates.
The existing stored-field modes are mandatory scalar T!, nullable T? with initial null, creation default T=expr, server-owned T server=expr, default-empty T[], and mandatory-array T[]!. Bare operation input types are already required. The replacement makes a bare stored scalar mandatory/non-null unless it has a default or server initializer, and disallows the redundant scalar bang. Nullable initialization, defaults, protected/server/secret fields, array [] initialization and []! input presence remain unchanged for models, contracts and events. Required creation data is not synthesized; absent update changes still differ from a submitted null. A lexical scan excluding strings/comments and != located 798 scalar markers and 18 mandatory-array markers.
Nullable member reads would use ?. only on a nullable receiver, yielding null for an absent receiver and otherwise performing ordinary type-checked and permission-respecting access. Failures are not converted to absence. Each nullable intermediate result requires another optional hop; regular dot needs a non-null value. Optionality propagates as one nullable type. No optional invocation, subscript or writable optional path is proposed. The fallback operator ?? accepts a nullable left operand and compatible right type, evaluates the left once and the right only on null. A non-null right removes result nullability; a nullable right keeps it. This replaces the coalesce builtin. ?? associates rightward at lower precedence than or, may not mix directly with and/or without parentheses, and must be grouped before arithmetic. A successful equality between safe-access output and a value statically known non-null proves the traversed receivers non-null for the true branch and following conjunction operands. Equality to null and inequality have no such true-continuation narrowing rule. Permission errors, invalid operations and truthiness are not weakened.
Planned source edits cover the 798 suffixes, four fallback calls with now or money(0,validated_currency), and three nullable event-result comparisons against non-null record IDs. Those fallback expressions are pure and cannot fail on the reviewed typed inputs; effects and access guards are not removed. Null result gives false for both the explicit non-null-and-equality form and optional equality; only true equality enables later result reads. Arithmetic/query grouping is retained, and unrelated null checks are left intact. The new explicit lazy fallback rule is not asserted equivalent to unspecified old evaluation for unreviewed calls. Extra operator grammar and flow facts require correct implementation, and these fragments have no compiler evidence. Evaluate missing or conflicting rules based on the actual proposal rather than stipulating preservation.
